title: Crimping Cobbles in Maple Canyon
summary:
We headed south out of Salt Lake City and found a dispersed campsite outside the town of Nephi. After finding a spot, I went for a run down a cow-infested forest service road. For dinner, we had some delicious Trader Joe's orange chicken and finished watching Iron Chef on Netflix, which we have been enjoying these last few weeks. Our destination in this part of Utah was Maple Canyon, a climbing area known for its conglomerate rock walls (basically vertical cobblestone streets). We pulled into our campsite, leveled our van to the best of our ability in a rather un-level spot, and immediately headed out to do some climbing. The next three days were some combination of the following in various orders: relax and read our books, go climbing (during which I would attempt, and never quite succeed, to send the route that I picked as a project for the week), cook a tasty dinner, spend more time reading, watch a movie or tv show. I also went on one extremely hot and extremely steep run while we were there, which was worth it for the great views at the top!

-Colin
